prediction.likelyOutcome: Barham is very likely to recover at least the $163,000 physical-taking valuation, since liability on that component is conceded and the only question is amount. The real variable is the access/easement claim: the trial court's considered denial of summary judgment on that theory, plus favorable language in the Agreed Order describing 'frontage along Threel Road' and an access-control line, gives Barham a genuinely triable — and better-than-even — shot at a meaningfully enhanced award, though the magnitude of that enhancement is not quantified anywhere in this record and will turn entirely on trial evidence (appraisal/expert testimony on diminution in value) not yet before this analysis.

issues.label: Compensability of Lost Threel Road Ingress-Egress Easement (Access/Easement Taking vs. Traffic-Flow Rule)
Carmel's Summary Judgment / Traffic-Flow Rule Defense

outcome.description: After a May 2022 jury trial the Marion Circuit Court entered judgment on a $2.4 million verdict for Barham and denied Carmel's motions to correct error, for new trial, and for remittitur. The Court of Appeals reversed on October 30, 2023, holding Barham had no compensable easement interest in Threel Road (already extinguished in the County Line condemnation) and that the access change was non-compensable under the ingress-egress and traffic-flow rules, and remanded with instructions to grant Carmel partial summary judgment on that issue.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
